text:
To decide which assay would be useless for learning about the mitochondrial actions of the new drug, ask whether the read-out in each case is a direct or at least meaningful proxy for mitochondrial function.

A. JC-1 dye (5,5',6,6'-Tetrachloro-1,1',3,3'-tetraethylbenzimidazolylcarbocyanine iodide) reports the mitochondrial membrane potential (ΔΨm). Flow cytometry after JC-1 staining is a classic, highly informative measure of mitochondrial activity. → Helpful.

B. Firefly luciferase uses ATP to convert luciferin into light. Luminescence from transfected cells therefore reports intracellular ATP, which in oxidative cells is produced largely by mitochondria. Although glycolysis also makes ATP, a fall or rise in total cellular ATP is still a good indicator of mitochondrial energetic status. → Helpful.

C. Mito-RTP (a MitoTracker-type redox-sensitive probe) specifically stains mitochondria and can reveal changes in mitochondrial number, morphology, or redox state by confocal microscopy. → Helpful.

D. Glucose-uptake assays quantify transport of glucose across the plasma membrane into whole cells; isolated mitochondria do not import glucose. Performing a glucose-uptake colorimetric assay on a mitochondrial pellet obtained by differential centrifugation would yield no meaningful information about mitochondrial function or the drug’s effect. → Not helpful.

Therefore the only experiment that will not help elucidate the mitochondrial role of the drug is option D.

Answer: D
